Request written confirmation that the deposit will be placed in a blocked account held in the tenant's name or jointly held. Keep a copy of the contract, the housing condition report (Wohnungszustandsprotokoll) signed upon move-in, and all correspondence with the landlord.
If the landlord notifies a rent increase or a change in the initial rent, the tenant has 30 days to file an objection with the rental conciliation authority of their district. The procedure is accessible without legal assistance, but in the case of substantial amounts or complexity, it is advisable to contact a free legal advice centre available in the main centres of the Canton or the tenant associations active at regional level.

item.description: Rental market in the canton of Thurgau: security deposit, cancellation, fee dispute and conciliation authority according to the Code of Obligations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Security deposit max 3 monthly rents on a blocked account in the tenant's name - Landlord's notice of termination valid only on the official cantonal form - Initial rent challenge within 30 days to the conciliation authority - Federal tenancy law (CO art. 253 ff.) identical in all cantons
## Key facts - **What**: federal rules on deposit, termination and initial rent challenge applicable in Thurgau - When: current provisions of the Code of Obligations - Where: Canton of Thurgau (and all of Switzerland) - Who: landlord, tenant, cantonal conciliation authority for tenancy matters - Amount: maximum deposit equal to 3 monthly rents - Deadline: 30 days to challenge the initial rent before the conciliation authority - Instrument: official cantonal form for landlord's notice of termination - Obligation: deposit account in the tenant's name, not the landlord's
Anyone renting an apartment in the Canton of Thurgau must deal with a residential market that reflects the canton's position in eastern Switzerland, between Constance and Zurich. The applicable law remains federal: the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO art. 253 ff.) sets out the rules on security deposits, termination and initial rent challenges uniformly across the national territory. Whatever the area — Frauenfeld, Kreuzlingen, Arbon, Amriswil or Weinfelden — tenant protections are the same as those provided in Zurich, Geneva or Basel.
The topic is of particular interest to workers and families moving into the canton, students in the Kreuzlingen area, and commuters operating in the Thurgau-St. Gallen-Ticino triangle who are looking for affordable housing.
### Security deposit and form of the contract
The deposit may not exceed three monthly rents (net rent without ancillary costs) and must be held in a bank or post office account in the tenant's name, not the landlord's. The owner may access it only in the case of justified rental claims. It is common to use an insurance policy or a blocked account managed by a bank: in both cases the money formally remains the tenant's. The lease agreement must clearly state the amount of the rent, the ancillary costs and the start date of the relationship.
### Landlord's notice of termination and official form
If the landlord intends to terminate the contract, federal law requires the use of the official form of the Canton of Thurgau, indicating the reason. The tenant has the right to request an extension of the notice period in case of family or financial difficulties.
The form must be completed in all its parts; a termination without justification or on a non-official form can be challenged before the conciliation authority for tenancy matters within 30 days of receipt. ## When the initial rent is excessive
Swiss tenancy law considers an initial rent abusive when it exceeds by more than 10% the comparable rents in the area, or when the landlord does not justify an increase compared to the previous rent. The authority responsible for assessing abuse is the conciliation authority for tenancy matters (Schlichtungsbehörde Mietrecht), a cantonal joint body made up of representatives of landlords and tenants, assisted by a chairperson.
### The contestation procedure
Within 30 days from the handover of the keys — or from the notification of a rent increase during the ongoing tenancy — the tenant may file an application for a rent reduction with the conciliation authority. The procedure is free of charge up to a certain threshold of disputed value and aims at an amicable settlement. If it fails, the decision can be appealed before the ordinary court.
The main tool available to the tenant is the comparison with comparable rents: the Federal Statistical Office (UST/BFS) periodically publishes data on average rents per canton and zone, useful as a reference. Federal legislation sets the framework, but tax multipliers and cantonal peculiarities can indirectly affect the level of rents.
### Example scenario
A tenant who enters into a new lease in a municipality in Thurgau and considers the rent higher than the reference values of the area may send an application for reduction to the conciliation authority within the legal deadline, attaching the relevant documentation. The procedure does not preclude the possibility of a direct agreement with the landlord: in many cases, mediation resolves the dispute before a formal decision is issued.
### Difference between contestation of the initial rent and reduction during the tenancy
The law distinguishes between the challenge of the initial rent (within 30 days from the handover) and the request for reduction during the ongoing tenancy, for example after an increase in ancillary costs or due to defects of the property. In both cases the rent must be based on comparable values: it is the tenant's burden to produce concrete elements (comparable listings, UST/BFS data, expert appraisals) to support their position.

item.description: How to obtain residence permit C in the Canton of Lucerne: years of residence, integration, language and application procedure.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Permit C: normally 10 years of residence in Switzerland, 5 for EU/EFTA citizens - Key criteria: integration, language knowledge, absence of debts with assistance - Application to the cantonal migration office of Lucerne via the municipality of residence - Possible early release in cases of merit or exceptional integration
## Key facts - **What**: Residence permit C (Long-term stay, indefinite) issued by the Canton of Lucerne according to the Federal Law on Foreigners (LStr) - Who: SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) at federal level, cantonal and municipal authority for implementation - When: Ordinary term after 10 years (5 years for EU/EFTA citizens) - Where: Canton Lucerne, cantonal migration office, via the municipality of residence - Requirements: Integration, language knowledge, economic conditions, good conduct, no social assistance debt - Documents: Valid passport, B permit, linguistic certificates, integration tests, certificate of domicile
In Switzerland, the residence permit C is the document that allows you to reside indefinitely and to exercise a lucrative activity without further authorizations. Issuance is governed by federal legislation on foreigners and supplemented by cantonal criteria: each canton, including Lucerne, can add specific conditions or timelines depending on the demographic and labour market situation.
## # To whom the ## What Lucerne concretely assesses
The canton examines five cumulative dimensions. The first is linguistic integration: for the Canton of Lucerne, both spoken and written knowledge of the language of the place of residence is required, normally German, with attestation through a recognised certificate (for example the FIDE test or equivalent). The required level is parameterised by the SEM according to the Common European Framework.
The second is social and professional integration: participation in economic life, renting or purchasing a home in the canton, enrolment of children in local schools, and absence of dependence on social assistance. The third concerns respect for public order: criminal records, pending judicial proceedings or significant fines may jeopardise the issuance of the permit.
The fourth dimension is economic: having sufficient income and not being burdened by debts to public assistance. The fifth is the duration of regular residence. The Canton of Lucerne, like all cantons, must also verify compliance with quotas and the labour market for third-country nationals.
### Early issuance and revocation: concrete scenarios
Federal legislation provides for the possibility of an early C permit on the basis of particular merits. Typical cases include: exceptional linguistic and social integration, outstanding professional or sporting activities, and family reunifications that justify it. The decision lies with the cantonal authority, in agreement with the SEM.
On the opposite side, the C permit may be revoked if the holder is durably dependent on social assistance, commits serious offences, or repeatedly violates public order. The revocation procedure follows cantonal administrative law with the right of appeal. The LAMal/KVG remains mandatory for every resident: health insurance must be taken out within three months of arrival or of changing canton, with premiums calculated by region and cantonal subsidies for those with modest incomes. To calculate net salary and social contributions — OASI/DI (AVS/AHV), occupational pension (LPP/BVG), and unemployment insurance (AD/AC) — the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) allows you to estimate the actual monthly amount.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Step-by-step procedure in Lucerne
The standard process involves four steps. First: gather the documentation. Valid passport or identity card, valid B permit, language certificate, certificate of residence issued by the municipality, proof of employment or financial self-sufficiency, and any extract from the Swiss criminal record.
Second: submit the application to the municipality of residence. The relevant municipal service checks the completeness of the documents and forwards them to the cantonal migration office of the Canton of Lucerne. Third: the cantonal office reviews the application and, for third-country nationals, coordinates with the SEM and SECO to ensure compliance with admission requirements. Fourth: written decision with notification; in case of rejection, an appeal can be filed within the time limits set by cantonal law.
### Deadlines, controls and impact on contributions
Once the C permit is obtained, no periodic renewals are required. Civil and tax obligations remain: every resident is subject to direct federal tax (IFD), cantonal and municipal tax, with an annual income declaration. The three levels — federal, cantonal and municipal — work in an integrated manner but are governed by separate laws: the AFC/ESTV for IFD and VAT, cantonal administrations for the cantonal and municipal portions. The [salary calculator](nav:calculator) helps estimate the monthly net amount including AVS/AI/IPG, ALV and LPP.
For those working in Switzerland, the payslip includes mandatory social contributions on the coordinated salary: AVS/AI/IPG 5.3% borne by the employee, ALV/AC 1.1% up to the indexed annual cap, LAINF/LAA between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. For the second pillar LPP/BVG, the minimum employee contributions are 7% from age 25 to 34, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, and 18% from age 55 until the reference retirement age. These values are defined at the federal level. For tax-related matters after the C permit is issued — registration with the municipality, choice of tax multiplier — it is useful to consult the [tax declaration](nav:tax-return).

item.title: The Post Office cuts jobs: up to 110 redundancies are expected
item.description: The Post Office plans to cut up to 110 jobs to reduce internal costs and finance the public service in the long term without public money.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Up to 110 jobs at risk - Cuts in management and support areas - No impact on post offices and delivery - Objective: to safeguard public service
## Key facts - **What**: Cut of internal jobs - When: Announced in a press release issued today, Monday - Where: In Switzerland, in the management and support sectors - Who: Swiss Post - Amount: Up to 110 positions affected
Swiss Post has officially announced the possibility of cutting up to 110 jobs. The main objective of this economic maneuver is to reduce internal costs in order to successfully finance the public service in the long term without having to resort in any way to taxpayers' money. The news was made public through an official press release issued on Monday. This decision is part of a structured corporate strategy developed on the basis of four well-defined fundamental pillars. These include proportionate tariff measures, the constant improvement of internal efficiency, targeted growth within the core business, and finally the modernization of established regulatory framework conditions. The economic and social context in which the entity operates is undergoing significant changes linked above all to customer habits. People are sending fewer and fewer paper letters and preferring to opt for online payments directly at the post office. The Post management itself wanted to specify that the growth recorded in other business sectors unfortunately is not sufficient to compensate for these structural contractions in traditional volumes. ### Statements from general management on future sustainability General Director Pascal Grieder publicly explained the motivations that pushed the company to make such a delicate decision for the workforce. His words clearly show the strategic vision of the Swiss postal entity. We have the responsibility to ensure that Swiss Post preserves its relevance, efficiency, and financial autonomy in the future as well. For this reason, we intend to reduce internal costs where they do not have a direct impact on customers, thus offering our contribution. The in-depth analysis of the announced maneuver highlights how the corporate reorganization will specifically and exclusively target certain administrative and support sectors. The staff cuts planned by company management will specifically affect management and internal logistic-administrative support areas. The company wanted to reassure users and operational staff by specifying that the measures currently under review do not in any way affect services dedicated directly to customers. Consequently, operational staff directly in contact with the public, such as those assigned to daily mail delivery or those employed in counter activities within branches scattered across the national territory, will not be affected by these staff reduction measures. This strategic choice makes it possible to safeguard the widespread presence of traditional postal service, focusing savings solely on top-level and management support structures that do not have a direct and daily impact on the use of services by citizens residing in Switzerland. ### The four-part strategy for financial autonomy and public service To fully understand the scope of the restructuring announced by Swiss Post, it is necessary to examine the four fundamental pillars on which the entire company strategic maneuver rests. The first pillar concerns the adoption of tariff measures that are defined as proportionate to the actual costs of the services offered. The second pillar focuses decisively on the continuous improvement of internal efficiency through the optimization of work processes. The third pillar provides for targeted growth focused exclusively on the company core business, trying to develop new revenue channels where the market offers favorable opportunities. The fourth and final pillar consists in the modernization of regulatory framework conditions, a fundamental aspect to allow the company to move agilely in a communication and postal services market that is increasingly digitized and competitive at a national level.

The issuance of the settlement permit C represents a fundamental milestone for foreign citizens residing in the Canton of Geneva who wish to establish a long-term presence on Swiss territory. Obtaining this title grants greater administrative and legal stability, bringing the foreign citizen closer to equal rights with Swiss residents, although the right to vote at the federal level remains excluded. The procedure requires the submission of detailed documentation demonstrating compliance with Swiss laws, the absence of tax debts or pending enforcement proceedings, and regular participation in the country's economic life.
### The federal and cantonal regulatory framework The Swiss system of permits for foreigners clearly distinguishes between short-term permits, temporary residence permits, and permanent settlement permits. In the Canton of Geneva, citizens from member countries of the European Union or the European Free Trade Association can usually aspire to the C permit after a continuous period of residence of five years, provided that integration is considered successful. For citizens of other states, the minimum duration ordinarily rises to ten years. The State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) establishes the general guidelines, but the investigation and examination of applications are the responsibility of the cantonal offices in charge of population and migration. Each stage of the request must be accurately documented, attaching extracts from the register of the Debt Collection and Bankruptcy Office and certificates attesting to the applicant's updated employment and income situation within the Genevan cantonal context. ### Integration and language criteria One of the central aspects for obtaining a C permanent residence permit in the Canton of Geneva involves demonstrating an adequate level of social and economic integration. The cantonal authorities verify that the applicant possesses sufficient language skills in the official language of the canton, namely French, according to the parameters recognized by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. This requirement aims to ensure that the individual can easily communicate with local institutions, carry out their professional activity, and integrate into the social fabric. In addition to language, respect for public order and security is examined, verifying the absence of serious criminal convictions or significant pending charges.
### Economic and social security aspects From an economic standpoint, the applicant must demonstrate that they do not depend on social assistance and are able to provide for their own maintenance and that of their dependent family members. This means having stable employment, either as an employee with regular payment of mandatory contributions to systems such as AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, or as a self-employed worker with a solid financial situation. The cantonal administrations analyze pay slips, tax returns managed through direct federal tax and the related cantonal and municipal taxes, as well as mandatory health insurance coverage through LAMal/KVG. item.title: Labour market in Switzerland: Seco confirms its solidity
item.description: The Swiss labour market remains solid despite uncertainties. Unemployment in August stands at 3.0%, with a seasonal increase among young people.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Unemployment rate at 3% in August - Increase among young people (15-24 years) to 3.4% - Confirmation of solidity by Jérôme Cosandey (Seco)
## Key facts - **What**: Unemployment data in Switzerland - When: August - Where: Switzerland - Who: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (Seco) - Amount: 3.0% total unemployment
The Swiss labor market as a whole continues to show resilience in a context still characterized by numerous geopolitical and economic uncertainties. This was stated by Jérôme Cosandey, head of the labor Directorate at the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (Seco), commenting in a teleconference on the unemployment data released in the morning by his officials.
### Official August data Official data released in August record an overall unemployment rate of 3.0%. The only significant increase concerns young people between 15 and 24 years of age, with the share of the unemployed rising to 3.4% in the eighth month of the year. This represents an increase of 0.6 percentage points compared to July, recording 2,400 more people for a total of 14,700 young people without a job. This dynamic is part of the general framework constantly monitored by the competent federal authorities for economy and employment throughout the national territory.
### Analysis of economic fluctuations According to the assessments expressed by the top management of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, the fluctuations recorded in the youth sector do not represent a structural trend reversal of the Swiss economy. On the contrary, the productive fabric continues to demonstrate a remarkable absorption capacity and overall resistance in the face of international tensions that continue to condition global financial and commercial markets. The general stability of employment remains a fundamental pillar for the economic and social well-being of the country, offering certainty to resident workers and businesses active in the various cantonal productive sectors. ### Seasonal dynamics for young people According to Jérôme Cosandey, the increase recorded among young people is an entirely normal seasonal phenomenon. Every summer, thousands of young people who have finished school, training or university enter the job market and have not yet found employment. The peak in unemployment in this segment is usually reached in August. The number of unemployed people among the under-20s then drops rapidly towards autumn, while for 20-25 year-olds the situation improves markedly with the start of the following year. The manager expressed confidence that this pattern will repeat itself on this occasion as well.
### Structural differences across age groups The data also confirms a significant structural difference within the Swiss labor market: young people are more exposed to the risk of being unemployed, but they find new employment much faster than older age groups. On average, for those under 25, it takes just over three months to leave the unemployment register, while for the over-55s it exceeds nine months. This difference in reintegration times highlights the different challenges that various generations face when looking for a new professional opportunity in the national economic context.
### The trend of short-time work Positive signals also come from short-time work. This tool, which allows companies to temporarily reduce working hours without proceeding with layoffs, is being used less and less. This trend confirms the overall resilience of the Swiss productive fabric, as concluded by Jérôme Cosandey during his economic analysis.

The differences between the age groups highlight the importance of exploiting the official channels and placement services available at the cantonal level in a timely manner.

The new national analysis led by stop2drop will for the first time quantify the presence of snus, nicotine pouches, and e-cigarettes in Swiss playgrounds. The survey will begin on Tuesday, September 8, and continue until September 22, involving 200 playgrounds across Switzerland. The collected data will be entered into an online questionnaire, analyzed by the organization, and published in November. The previous analysis, conducted in 2024, covered 170 playgrounds and collected over 15,000 cigarette butts, with an average of 91 per playground. According to stop2drop, the results confirm that littering of tobacco and nicotine products is not a marginal phenomenon but a widespread issue in spaces intended for children. Cigarette butts are not harmless waste, as they can contain up to 7,000 chemical substances, and if ingested, can cause poisoning, a particularly relevant risk in places where children play, touch the ground, and easily bring their hands to their mouths. Stop2drop's attention is not only focused on abandoned waste but also on the consumption of nicotine products near children. The organization reminds that passive smoking is harmful even outdoors, and children are particularly sensitive to the substances contained in tobacco smoke. The press release also cites a scientific review indicating that children who grow up exposed to parental or sibling smoking have up to three times the probability of starting to smoke during childhood or adolescence. For stop2drop, making playgrounds free of smoking and nicotine therefore means intervening both on the health and prevention fronts. The issue also has an economic dimension. "Even just for cleanup, municipalities spend over 52 million Swiss francs every year", emphasizes Markus Dick, director of stop2drop. The figure refers to the costs of cleaning up littering waste in Switzerland and includes various fractions of waste, not just cigarette butts. ### Health and Safety Implications The presence of nicotine products in playgrounds poses a serious health risk to children. Cigarettes, nicotine pouches, and e-cigarettes can contain up to 7,000 chemical substances, some of which are highly toxic. If children ingest these products, they can suffer poisoning that may have serious consequences for their health. Additionally, passive smoking is harmful even outdoors, and children are particularly sensitive to the substances contained in tobacco smoke. A scientific review cited by stop2drop indicates that children who grow up exposed to their parents' or siblings' smoking have up to three times the probability of starting to smoke during childhood or adolescence. This underscores the importance of keeping playgrounds free of smoking and nicotine to protect children's health and prevent smoking initiation.
### Economic Implications The littering of nicotine products in playgrounds also has a significant economic dimension. Municipalities spend over 52 million Swiss francs annually on cleaning up litter generated by littering. This figure includes various fractions of waste, not just cigarette butts, and highlights the extent of the problem. Additionally, the presence of nicotine products in playgrounds can influence the perception of adults and visitors of public spaces, potentially reducing the attractiveness of these areas for tourism and commerce. The collected data will be analyzed and published in November, providing up-to-date and accurate information on the current situation. Additionally, stop2drop has introduced new signage to distinguish smoke-free and nicotine-free playgrounds. So far, 24 Swiss municipalities have decided to join the initiative. The signage aims to make the municipalities' commitment visible and remind adults that playgrounds are primarily places for children. A new coordinated campaign is planned for the spring of 2027. Additionally, citizens can contribute to the survey by analyzing the playground in their neighborhood between 8 and 22 September. item.description: Ignazio Cassis explains that every war is different and that Switzerland cannot condemn the actions of the United States without demonstrating concrete facts.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Switzerland does not impose sanctions on the United States for the attack on Iran - Every war is different, says Ignazio Cassis - Switzerland could lose friendly relations with other countries
## Key facts - **What**: Interview of Ignazio Cassis on neutrality and sanctions - When: September 27, 2024 - Where: Bern - Who: Ignazio Cassis, federal councilor - Amount: Not specified
In a face-to-face interview live from Bern, federal councilor Ignazio Cassis answered questions from the 20 Minuten editorial team and readers on the neutrality initiative, which is up for a vote on September 27. The central theme of the exchange was the price Switzerland might have to pay, internationally, depending on the outcome of the vote, with an eye already on the parallel dossier of treaties with the European Union. ### Sanctions against Russia and not the United States Cassis excludes that a yes to the initiative would expose Switzerland to direct sanctions, as he believes it would not constitute a violation of international law. However, the price would be paid elsewhere: "But they will be less accommodating and much less friendly towards us; relations will cool off. This is as certain as death and taxes," he said. On the military front, it is even clearer: in case of acceptance, cooperation with NATO would be "clearly" limited. Sanctions by the UN would also theoretically remain possible, but the veto power of the great powers would make them effectively unenforceable against Russia, the United States, or China. On the sanctions already in place against Moscow, Cassis defends a considered decision: "Such a violation of international law cannot be simply condemned; we must prove with concrete facts that we cannot accept it." When asked why other countries, such as the United States for the attack on Iran, are not sanctioned in the same way, he replies: "A good question, which allows me to say that every war is different." He recalls that the UN has also not intervened, blocked by the American veto, and that Swiss law only allows autonomous sanctions if imposed by the UN or the main commercial partners, i.e., the EU; Bern has nevertheless condemned the raid on Tehran and suspended arms supplies to Washington. ### International situation "very difficult" Cassis emphasizes the relationship with Brussels the most. The parliamentary debate on the bilateral treaties with the EU will take place in the fall, and for the federal councilor, stable and calm relations with the neighbors are of crucial importance today, in a context that he describes without equivocation: "The geopolitical situation is changing rapidly, and not necessarily in the right direction." The rules that protect Switzerland, he adds, "are increasingly being questioned," in what he describes as a "very difficult" historical phase. When pressed on his possible departure from government before the popular vote on the EU treaties, Cassis does not commit: "If I knew when this referendum would be held, I could give an answer," he said, thus avoiding confirming or denying a possible re-election in 2027. As for the accusation, coming from Moscow and Zelensky, of a lost neutrality, Cassis replies that the Russian reaction was "obviously predictable" from a sanctioned state, while on the Ukrainian charge, he limits himself to a laconic: "I do not know exactly what they are referring to." ### Practical Implications for Switzerland The interview with Ignazio Cassis highlights the potential consequences of the vote on the initiative for neutrality. If Switzerland were to adopt a neutral stance, it could face several challenges, including the loss of friendly relations with other countries and the limitation of military cooperation with NATO. Additionally, Switzerland might have to deal with UN sanctions, although the veto power of major powers would make them effectively inapplicable against Russia, the United States, or China.
### Comparison with Other Nations Switzerland does not impose sanctions on the United States for the attack on Iran, unlike other countries. Cassis explains that every war is different and that Switzerland cannot simply condemn the actions of the United States without demonstrating concrete facts. This balanced approach could influence Switzerland's position in the future, especially in a rapidly evolving geopolitical context.

## In a nutshell - The BepiColombo mission is about to enter the crucial phase of insertion into the orbit of Mercury - ESA and JAXA launched the mission in October 2018 - Mercury's orbit is scheduled for November 21
## Key facts - What: Insertion into the orbit of Mercury - When: October 2018 (launch), November 21 (orbit) - Where: Mercury - Who: ESA and JAXA - Amount: 10 billion kilometres travelled
After eight years of travel and more than 10 billion kilometers traveled, the BepiColombo mission is entering the most delicate phase of its long journey to Mercury, the smallest and least known of the planets in the Solar System. The joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Space Agency (JAXA) will begin an unprecedented exploration of the planet closest to the Sun in April. The European probe MPO (Mercury Planet Orbiter) will study Mercury from just 480 kilometers above sea level, while the Japanese probe Mio will analyze its space environment and magnetic field following an elliptical orbit that will take it up to 11,000 kilometers from the surface. The University of Bern is also actively involved in the project, having led the creation of two scientific instruments: the Strofio mass spectrometer, intended to analyse Mercury's thin atmosphere, and the Bela laser altimeter, which will allow three-dimensional images of the planet's surface to be obtained.
📊 Data ### The crucial phase of orbital insertion
Before starting the data collection, however, BepiColombo must face a complex phase of orbital insertion. According to the ESA, this is a series of high-risk operations, made particularly difficult by the extreme conditions of Mercury, where temperatures oscillate between -180 and 450 degrees Celsius and solar radiation is particularly intense. The Bela probe, developed by the University of Bern, was sent into space in 2018 and is now preparing for its crucial mission. The separation of the two probes from the transfer module was a fundamental milestone achieved successfully, with the two probes separating autonomously from the spacecraft. The ESA confirmed the success of the operation, which took almost two hours to communicate due to the distance of approximately 200 million kilometers from Earth.
📊 **Technical and operational data** The BepiColombo mission, a joint project of the ESA and the Japanese Space Agency (JAXA), has an estimated cost of 1.8 billion euros. The Bela probe, developed by the University of Bern, weighs approximately 110 kilograms and has a diameter of 1.5 meters. The orbital insertion phase is scheduled for December 2025, after a seven-year journey.
💡 Survival strategies To face the extreme conditions of Mercury, BepiColombo is equipped with an advanced thermal protection system, which includes a ceramic thermal shield and an active cooling system. Additionally, the probe is equipped with an autonomous navigation system, which allows it to correct its course without direct intervention from operators on Earth.
⚠️ Risks and challenges One of the main risks of the mission is the possible emission of dust from the surface of Mercury, which could damage the probe's sensors. Additionally, intense solar radiation could affect the operation of electronic instruments. To mitigate these risks, scientists have developed emergency protocols that include the temporary suspension of operations and the restart of systems only after verifying their integrity.
🌍 Swiss context Switzerland plays a crucial role in the BepiColombo mission, with the University of Bern contributing to the development of the Bela probe. Additionally, Switzerland is an important center for space research, with the presence of companies such as RUAG Space, which has provided components for the mission. Switzerland is also a founding member of the ESA, contributing with 220 million euros per year to the agency's budget.
📊 Comparison with other missions The BepiColombo mission is similar to other space missions, such as the Mariner 10 mission of the '70s, which provided the first detailed images of Mercury. However, BepiColombo is the first mission to study Mercury with advanced instruments and for an extended period, thanks to a stable orbit and an advanced thermal protection system.
💡 Future prospects The BepiColombo mission has the potential to revolutionize our understanding of Mercury and the solar system. The data collected could provide new information on the formation of the planet and its evolution, as well as the effects of solar radiation and dust on the surface. Additionally, the mission could open new opportunities for space research, with Switzerland continuing to play a key role in the sector.

item.description: The September 27 vote on Swiss neutrality: what it means and what the implications are for the country's future.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - On September 27, a vote will be held on the initiative on Swiss neutrality. - The initiative proposes permanent and armed neutrality. - Swiss neutrality is already guaranteed, but the initiative wants to establish clear principles in the Constitution.
## Key facts - **What**: Vote on the initiative on Swiss neutrality. - When: September 27. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Luca Frasa, Movimento giovani Leghisti. - Amount: Not specified.
On September 27, Swiss citizens will be called to the polls to vote on the initiative on neutrality. Luca Frasa, of Movimento giovani Leghisti, has declared that he will vote decisively YES to the initiative. According to Frasa, Swiss neutrality does not mean isolation, but the ability to speak with all without belonging to anyone. A Switzerland that collaborates, trades, dialogues and helps, but that preserves the freedom to decide according to its own interests and tradition.
Swiss neutrality already exists and will continue to exist even in case of a No vote. However, the initiative proposes to establish clear and lasting principles in the Constitution. The initiative proposes permanent and armed neutrality, excludes membership in military alliances except in the case of an attack on Switzerland and sets limits on participation in coercive measures against belligerent states, maintaining obligations arising from the UN. At the same time, it assigns to the Confederation the task of using its neutrality to prevent and resolve conflicts and offer its good offices.
### The strength of the project
For Luca Frasa, the strength of the project lies in its ability to maintain Switzerland's independence. Neutrality does not mean indifference, but independence. Switzerland can condemn an aggression and a violation of international law, help the victims of a war, support humanitarian action and defend its values, without becoming part of one of the blocs that are forming in the world.
### Limits and interpretations
Opponents of the initiative argue that it would limit the maneuvering room of the Federal Council. True, but is it really a sufficient argument to say No? Credible neutrality must be predictable. If the interpretation changes according to the conflict, international pressures or the political majority of the moment, it risks losing the trust of others in its particular position. ## Practical Implications
The initiative on Swiss neutrality has significant practical implications for the future of the country. Establishing clear and lasting principles in the Constitution could ensure greater stability and predictability in Swiss foreign policy. This could influence diplomatic relations, international collaborations, and Switzerland's participation in coercive measures against belligerent states.
### Prevention and Resolution of Conflicts
The initiative assigns the Confederation the task of using its neutrality to prevent and resolve conflicts. This could mean a more active role for Switzerland in international diplomacy, offering its good offices to mediate between conflicting parties. This role could strengthen Switzerland's reputation as a neutral and reliable mediator.
### Limitations on Participation in Coercive Measures
The initiative places limits on Switzerland's participation in coercive measures against belligerant states. This could influence Switzerland's ability to participate in international sanctions or other coercive measures. However, the initiative maintains obligations arising from the UN, ensuring that Switzerland can still fulfill its international obligations.
### Impact on Foreign Policy
Establishing clear and lasting principles in the Constitution could influence Switzerland's long-term foreign policy. Permanent and armed neutrality could ensure greater stability and predictability in Switzerland's international relations. This could influence the decisions of the Federal Council and Parliament in matters of foreign policy.

Costa Rica is among the countries with the highest use of pesticides in the world. Especially on the Caribbean coast, abundant rainfall carries residues from agricultural lands into drainage canals and rivers, reaching aquatic and coastal ecosystems.

Pesticides reach the aquatic systems where the tadpoles grow, to which the frog’s life remains linked. item.title: The world of cars is getting greyer and greyer and it's not just an impression
item.description: According to an analysis by the Federal Office of Roads, red was the most popular colour for new registrations in 1985, with almost 23%. Today that share has dropped to 4%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The world of cars has become increasingly grey. - In 1985, red was the most popular color for new registrations, with nearly 23%. - Today, red represents only 4% of new registrations. - Blue represents 9%, green 5%. - 80% of cars are dominated by grey, black, and white.
## Key facts - **What**: The world of cars has become more grey. - When: From 1985 to today. - Where: Switzerland. - Who: Federal Roads Office (Astra). - Amount: 23% in 1985, 4% today.
The world of cars has become increasingly grey, and it's not just an impression. The reasons for this chromatic uniformity range from the minimalism in vogue to the lower costs of standard colors offered by car manufacturers.
ZURICH - Those who have the impression that a few decades ago the Swiss car fleet was much more colorful are not wrong. According to a special analysis carried out by the Federal Roads Office (Astra) for the media outlets of the Tamedia group, in 1985 red was the most popular color for new registrations, with nearly 23%. Today, that share has been reduced to 4%. Blue represents 9%, green 5%. The remaining 80% is dominated by three 'non-colors': grey, black, and white. In 1996, these shades covered just a third of the total.
### The phenomenon is global According to the paint manufacturer Axalta, only 20% of cars worldwide have vibrant colors. In an article published today on the online site of the Tages-Anzeiger (TA), Michael Baumann, of Amag, the largest Swiss importer, explains the trend with the customers' preference for timeless and widely appreciated colors.
As for the heat accumulated by dark surfaces, the company does not foresee an abandonment of black for climatic reasons: the internal temperature depends more on windows and air conditioning than on the color of the bodywork. According to the expert, the trend is not destined to change: bright colors like orange or green appear in advertisements or on sports models but are purchased much less than neutral colors. At most, subdued shades of green, blue, and natural colors could gain ground.
The Astra data show slight gender differences: women, who are registered owners of 37% of vehicles, have a more pronounced preference than men for purple, orange, and red, but they also choose grey, black, and white in the majority.
Monochromy does not only concern the roads. An analysis by the online retailer Galaxus cited by TA reveals that black clothing has gone from 33% in 2019 to over 43%. Those under 30 are the most faithful to the dark look: 60% of the items purchased are black. Consequently, the retailer orders more and more black items. Even IKEA sofas have progressively narrowed down to neutral colors like white, grey, and beige.
The phenomenon is historical: a study by the Science Museum in London on 7000 photographs of everyday objects from the last two centuries shows that color has given way to a dominant anthracite, while shapes have become more square and uniform. According to Therese Hänni, director of the Koloristika training center in Bern, current fashion rewards minimalism and durability: 'A winter coat in a basic shade is used longer than a pink one, and neutral pieces match better,' she explains in statements reported by TA. For young people, black is a uniform that does not expose them to judgment: 'In a phase of searching for their own identity, they do not want to stand out but to adapt. Group pressure determines choices.' In the past, youth groups were much more colorful. Hänni adds a psychological aspect. 'Color, for many, appears less valuable. Black or brown gives the idea of an expensive piece. Luxury is never orange, which seems cheap and noisy.' The only exception remains sports: in skiing or cycling, bright colors persist. As for a possible return to variety, Hänni is categorical: 'The lack of boldness in fashion and consumers will keep us prisoners of black, gray, and brown for a long time.' Among those commenting online on the news, there are also much more pragmatic reasons to explain the situation in the automotive sector, dictated by supply influencing demand. 'If gray or white are cheap and immediately available, while a custom color costs several hundred or over a thousand francs more, many buyers do not choose gray out of passion but because of the price and availability,' observes a user. ### Practical implications The trend towards neutral colours such as grey, black and white has practical implications for Swiss consumers. Automakers offer standard colors at lower costs than custom colors, influencing buyers' choices. This phenomenon is not only limited to cars, but also extends to clothing and furnishings, where neutral colours are increasingly predominant.
### Comparison with the previous situation In 1985, red was the most popular colour for new registrations, with almost 23%. Today, that share has dropped to 4%. Blue accounts for 9%, green for 5%. The remaining 80% is dominated by grey, black and white. This change reflects a global trend towards neutral and timeless colours.
### Future scenarios According to Michael Baumann of Amag, the trend towards neutral colours is not going to change. Bright tints such as orange or green appear in advertisements or on sports models, but are purchased much less than neutral colors. At most, they could gain terrain sober shades of green, blue, and natural colors.
### Gender differences The Astra data show slight gender differences: women, who own 37% of cars, have a more marked preference than men for purple, orange and red, but they also choose mostly grey, black and white. This indicates that the preference for neutral colors is transversal to both genders.

It is advisable to inquire with car manufacturers about the cost and availability of custom colours.

item.description: The sale of cannabis in pharmacies in Bern, Biel and Lucerne favors less risky consumption, according to a study.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Selling cannabis in pharmacies in Bern, Biel and Lucerne reduces the risks. - The pilot project is ongoing from 2024 and extended until October 2028. - Prices are slightly higher than on the black market.
## Key facts - **What**: Sale of cannabis in pharmacies. - When: From 2024, extended until October 2028. - Where: Bern, Biel and Lucerne. - Who: University of Bern and Lucerne. - Amount: Prices slightly higher than the black market.
The sale of cannabis in pharmacies in Bern, Biel and Lucerne is proving to favour less risky consumption. This is what emerges from an interim scientific evaluation of a pilot project, presented today in Bern by the three cities involved. The study called "Script" of the Universities of Bern and Lucerne involves 1,177 people. In the nine pharmacies involved, specialist staff inform customers about harm-reducing modes of consumption, such as vaping or oral intake instead of smoking. 71% of respondents passed these tips on to people in their entourage.
### Pricing and Consulting The prices are slightly higher than those on the black market, which helps, among other things, to finance the consultancy activity. While older people accept prices, young people between the ages of 18 and 25 react more sensitively. The management of the study sees this as an effective tool for the protection of minors.
### Results ## Practical Implications The sale of cannabis in pharmacies could have significant public health implications. Specialized advice offered in pharmacies could reduce the risks associated with cannabis use, such as breathing problems related to smoking. In addition, slightly higher prices on the black market could help fund further advisory and prevention activities.
### Comparison with the Black Market The black market is often associated with lower quality products and riskier consumption practices. Regulated pharmacy sales could offer a safer and more controlled alternative. This could also reduce the number of consumers turning to the black market, improving the overall quality of cannabis consumption.
### Future of Regulation The positive results of the pilot project could influence future legislation. If regulated sale in pharmacies proves effective in reducing risks, there may be greater support for a federal law regulating access to cannabis. This could lead to greater safety and quality in cannabis consumption across Switzerland.
